name: context7-codex
description: Look up Context7 library documentation and code examples on demand.
usage: Use resolve-library-id to locate a library, then query-docs to search it. If the user supplies an exact library ID, query it directly.
config: The apiKey in this plugin's private JSON may be empty for anonymous access or set to a key.

name: exa-codex
description: Search for sources and read web pages with Exa on demand.
usage: Use web_search_exa to find sources and web_fetch_exa to read a specific page. Legacy calls with only query remain supported; the default objective is the first 4096 characters of query.
config: Set apiKey in this plugin's private JSON before making a live call.

name: tavily-codex
description: Search, extract, crawl, and conduct research with Tavily on demand.
usage: Use search/extract for finding and extracting pages; map/crawl for a defined site scope; research when the task calls for synthesis across sources. Check the original task and usage before expanding the scope.
config: Set apiKey in this plugin's private JSON before making a live call.

name: microsoft-learn-codex
description: Look up official Microsoft Learn documentation and code examples on demand.
usage: Use microsoft_docs_search for official documentation, microsoft_code_sample_search for code examples, and microsoft_docs_fetch for a relevant full document. Connects to https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp.

name: fetch-codex
description: Read web pages on demand through the official Python Fetch MCP server.
usage: fetch preserves the official Markdown, robots, raw, max_length, and start_index pagination behavior. Follow the result guidance to continue after truncation; pass raw: true when the original page is needed.
config: No key is required. uvx must be on PATH. The first live call runs uvx --from mcp-server-fetch==2026.8.18 mcp-server-fetch and prepares the pinned official package. The Python backend closes with the gateway.

name: sequential-thinking-codex
description: Use the official core for stepwise analysis with revisions and branches.
usage: sequentialthinking supports revisions, branches, boolean strings, and history. Call it only when the task needs explicit stepwise analysis; history lasts for the current gateway lifetime.
config: No key is required. The first call loads the official 2026.8.31 core and Chalk 5.6.2 into the current Node process, without another Node backend or installer; thought logging is disabled. Pinned sources, adaptation hashes, and licenses are in vendor/sequential-thinking.
